passage: Nitin sat on the flat's living room floor and piled up wooden blocks, one on another: one, two, three, four, five, six. At the sixth the tower toppled with a clatter. Farhan, Nitin's older cousin, looked up from his book. Nitin did not cry or complain, only said "Again," and built it once more, this time with the long block first and the small ones later. It grew to seven before it fell.

qa.q: How many blocks were in the tower when it fell the first time?
qa.a: The tower fell when the sixth block went on.

qa.q: What was Nitin feeling after the tower toppled?
qa.a: Nitin was calm and determined, since there was no crying and only "Again," and the rebuild started right away.

qa.q: What alternative approach could help Nitin build higher, and why?
qa.a: Nitin could ask Farhan how he would stack the blocks, or make the bottom wider, because a small change to the base can matter more than luck.

qa.q: How might Farhan see Nitin's way of building?
qa.a: Farhan sees a patient child trying a new order each time; he keeps reading instead of stepping in, which suggests he trusts Nitin to work it out.

grounding: A child stacks blocks into a tower, watches it fall at the sixth, and builds again with the blocks in a slightly different order.
